items.claim: This one-verse leviathan judgment is a genuinely self-contained proclamation, opening its own in-that-day formula distinct from the imperative hiding oracle before it and from the vineyard song's own fresh song-frame onset after it, with parashah breaks corroborating both edges.
items.evidence: Isa.27.1 opens בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא יִפְקֹ֣ד (byte tier) addressing a third-person sea-monster, while the very next verse opens its own repeated in-that-day formula, בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (byte tier), shifting to a vocative song-summons and then first-person divine speech -- two adjacent but formally distinct proclamations rather than one continuous speech; single-witness setumah marks close the unit on both sides.

items.claim: The vineyard-song reprise is rightly bounded as its own unit: it opens on its own song-summons formula distinct from Isa.27.1's onset, and the first-person divine keeper-speech running through the verse closing at Isa.27.5 gives way to third-person report at Isa.27.6, where none of the sustained first-person forms recur.
items.evidence: בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (byte tier) opens the song; אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ נֹֽצְרָ֔הּ (byte tier) begins the first-person divine speech continuing to the suffixed forms closing Isa.27.5; Isa.27.6 opens instead with הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (byte tier), third-person report carrying no first-person marker.

items.claim: Binding Isa.27.6-11 into one unit is grammatically warranted beyond the pronoun-chain point already given: the fortified-city judgment of Isa.27.10-11 is explicitly subordinated to Jacob's atonement of Isa.27.9 by the causal clause opening Isa.27.10, so the foil functions inside the same argument rather than opening an independent unit that Isa.27.12's fresh in-that-day formula would then have to compete with.
items.evidence: Isa.27.10 opens with the causal כִּ֣י עִ֤יר (byte tier), grammatically tying the city's desolation to the preceding atonement clause rather than introducing an unrelated topic; Isa.27.12 opens instead with its own fresh formula, וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יַחְבֹּ֧ט (byte tier), outside this row's span.

items.claim: Splitting the threshing proclamation from its trumpet-summons neighbor matches the structural pattern of Isaiah's own repeated onset formulas, where a fresh formula-opening with a distinct image marks a distinct proclamation rather than a continuation, matching how 5:8, 5:11, 5:18, 5:20, 5:21, and 5:22 each open a fresh verse-initial onset for what are read as distinct woe-proclamations.
items.evidence: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יַחְבֹּ֧ט (byte tier) opens Isa.27.12 with its own formula and image (threshing); Isa.27.13 repeats the formula with a different image (trumpet); single-witness setumah marks close both Isa.27.11 and Isa.27.12.

items.claim: Treating this verse as a self-contained proclamation is correctly anchored on two different kinds of edges: its own in-that-day onset internally, and the fixed larger-unit boundary into Isa.28.1 externally -- the latter holding regardless of how the former is argued, since no woe, oracle-header, or divine-speech formula opens Isa.28.1 as a continuation of this verse's content.
items.evidence: וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (byte tier) opens the verse; Isa.28.1 opens instead on a distinct woe-cry over Ephraim's drunkards, a different addressee and topic sharing no vocabulary or formula with this verse.

items.claim: Holding Isa.28.1-13 together as one woe_oracle is warranted beyond the crown-phrase echo already cited: the priest-and-prophet turn at Isa.28.7 opens with a conjunctive 'and also these,' not any tier-1 onset formula, so it continues the same indictment voice rather than restarting the unit.
items.evidence: Isa.28.7 opens with וְגַם אֵ֨לֶּה֙ (byte tier), a continuative link rather than a hoy, massa, or koh-amar onset; the crown-of-pride phrase itself recurs at the accent-stripped tier between עֲטֶ֤רֶת גֵּאוּת֙ (Isa.28.1, byte tier there) and עֲטֶ֥רֶת גֵּא֖וּת (Isa.28.3, byte tier there), each byte-identical to its own verse and accent-stripped-identical to the other, matching the tier the row itself names.

items.claim: The high confidence rating for holding Isa.28.14-22 as one unbroken unit understates the live rival at the Isa.28.16 koh-amar divine-speech frame, which the row rejects with only a generic addressee-continuity claim rather than the stronger subordinating evidence actually available in the bytes.
items.evidence: Isa.28.16 opens with לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ (byte tier): the causal 'therefore' directly ties the koh-amar formula to Isa.28.15's covenant-with-death quotation as its answer, which is a stronger warrant for keeping the two together than the reason the row gives, yet neighboring rows in this same stretch facing comparably live internal-split rivals (the crown-reversal rival at Isa.28.5-6, the pronoun-antecedent rival at Isa.27.6-7) settle at medium or medium-low rather than high, so this row's confidence sits above the pattern its own evidence supports.

items.claim: The trial_speech label is a properly disclosed operative-category application rather than a referent decision: the doubled summons pair opening Isa.28.23 is a genuine fresh vocative distinct from the preceding cornerstone unit's own frame, and the unit closes cleanly on the chapter's last verse before the fresh woe onset that opens Isa.29.1.
items.evidence: הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ (byte tier) doubles the summons verb pair at the very opening of Isa.28.23, a vocative-onset device distinct from the koh-amar frame closing at Isa.28.22; Isa.29.1 opens on its own doubled woe-cry, a verse-initial hoy onset outside this row's span.
